module_title: Discharge of Surety, Irrevocable Agency, and Sub-Agents
introduction: Tailored for advanced legal exams and UPSC Law Optional, this level covers the complex mechanisms by which a surety is discharged from liability, the delicate difference between a sub-agent and a substituted agent, and instances where an agency cannot be revoked.

core_concepts.title: Discharge of Surety (Sections 133-139)
core_concepts.description:
A surety is discharged (freed from liability) under specific circumstances, heavily tested in exams:
- Variance in Terms (Sec 133): Any change made in the terms of the contract between the creditor and debtor without the surety's consent discharges the surety for future transactions.
- Release of Principal Debtor (Sec 134): If the creditor legally releases the debtor, the surety is also discharged.
- Compounding with Debtor (Sec 135): If the creditor makes a settlement with the debtor to give them more time, the surety is discharged.
- *Exception*: Mere forbearance to sue (the creditor just delays suing the debtor) does NOT discharge the surety (Sec 137).

core_concepts.title: Rights of Surety: Subrogation and Indemnity
core_concepts.description:
- Right of Subrogation (Sec 140): Once the surety pays off the debtor's debt, they step into the shoes of the creditor and inherit all rights the creditor had against the principal debtor.
- Implied Indemnity (Sec 145): In every guarantee, there is an implied promise by the principal debtor to indemnify the surety for any sum rightfully paid.

core_concepts.title: Sub-Agent vs. Substituted Agent
core_concepts.description:
The general rule is *Delegatus non potest delegare* (a delegate cannot further delegate). 
- Sub-Agent (Sec 191): Employed by the original agent. The principal is bound by the acts of the sub-agent, but the sub-agent is responsible ONLY to the original agent, not the principal.
- Substituted Agent (Sec 194): An agent names another person to act for the principal in the business of agency. Once named and accepted, this person becomes a direct agent of the principal, and the original agent drops out of the picture.

core_concepts.title: Irrevocable Agency (Agency Coupled with Interest)
core_concepts.description:
Generally, a principal can revoke an agency at any time before the authority is exercised (Sec 201). 
- Exception (Sec 202): Where the agent has an interest in the property forming the subject matter of the agency, the agency CANNOT be terminated to the prejudice of such interest. (e.g., Principal owes Agent 1 Lakh. Principal gives Agent authority to sell his land and recover the debt from the sale proceeds. Principal cannot revoke this agency).

important_entities.name: Ratification (Section 196-200)
important_entities.significance: If an agent acts without authority, the principal can ratify it later. However, ratification must be of the *whole* transaction (cannot ratify only the profitable part), and it cannot injure a third party.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: If there are multiple co-sureties, does releasing one co-surety by the creditor discharge the others? **NO (Sec 138)**. A release of one co-surety does not discharge the others, nor does it free the released surety from their responsibility to the other co-sureties.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Remember VRC to recall the active actions by a Creditor that will legally discharge a Surety from their obligation.

exam_strategy_tips: In CLAT PG or Judiciary Mains, if asked about 'Agency Coupled with Interest', immediately quote **Section 202**, state that it is an Irrevocable Agency, and provide the classic example of debt recovery through sale.
